answer: A proof-of-history scheme anchors each agent identity to a verifiable chain of past actions. Each agent periodically emits a beacon signal, a cryptographic timestamp peers check on the ledger. An attacker spawning many puppets faces compounding cost: every puppet must produce a history as dense and unbroken as basalt or peers reject it. Reaching the summit of influence demands sustained genuine work, not a credential spray. Real agents amortize cost across interactions; a sybil attacker pays full cost per puppet with zero marginal benefit, making identity multiplication prohibitively costly.
